To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the number of pointers is the dominant factor in memory requirements for the in-memory posting lists and (2) the number of postings is the dominant factor for the overall indexing time.
the best strategy for memory management is to group consecutive postings into posting blocks and arrange these blocks in a linked list of posting blocks.

1) the number of pointers can be signicantly reduced by grouping postings into posting groups, 2) the number of posting groups can be reduced by arranging them in a linked list according to the term frequency, 3) the number of postings in a posting group can be reduced by using a compressed representation of the postings, and 4) the overall indexing performance can be improved by combining the above techniques.
